title: Outage: a worker node NotReady after patching, and a drain to do

objective: Troubleshoot clusters and nodes: a NotReady node, kubelet configuration and certificates, the container runtime and the node's conditions with kubectl describe node, journalctl -u kubelet and crictl
secondaryObjectives: Manage the lifecycle of a cluster: upgrade the control plane and then each node with kubeadm upgrade, drain, kubelet and kubectl upgrades, and uncordon, one minor version at a time

Prepare the underlying infrastructure for a kubeadm cluster: container runtime (containerd) with the systemd cgroup driver, kernel modules and sysctls, swap off, and the ports the control plane and kubelet need

Relevant text: 'In the case that a node becomes unreachable ... the node controller sets the Ready condition to Unknown'; 'By default, the node controller waits 5 minutes between marking the node as Unknown and submitting the first eviction request'; heartbeats are updates to the Node's .status and Lease objects in kube-node-lease; 'Marking a node as unschedulable prevents the scheduler from placing new pods onto that Node but does not affect existing Pods on the Node. This is useful as a preparatory step before a node reboot or other maintenance.' Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.

Relevant text: 'node.kubernetes.io/not-ready: Node is not ready. This corresponds to the NodeCondition Ready being False'; 'Kubernetes automatically adds a toleration for node.kubernetes.io/not-ready and node.kubernetes.io/unreachable with tolerationSeconds=300 ... Pods remain bound to Nodes for 5 minutes after one of these problems is detected.' DaemonSet pods tolerate them with no tolerationSeconds. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation (v1.37), Installing kubeadm: Swap configuration
sources.note: Relevant text: 'The default behavior of a kubelet is to fail to start if swap memory is detected on a node.' 'To disable swap, sudo swapoff -a can be used to disable swapping temporarily. To make this change persistent across reboots, make sure swap is disabled in config files like /etc/fstab, systemd.swap'. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11. The kubelet's exact log wording in the scenario is an authored rendering.

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Safely Drain a Node, and the kubectl drain reference
sources.note: Relevant text: drain lets you 'safely evict all of your pods from a node before you perform maintenance'; safe evictions 'will respect the PodDisruptionBudgets you have specified'; 'Any drains that would cause the number of healthy replicas to fall below the specified budget are blocked'; 'kubectl uncordon <node name>' afterwards. kubectl drain reference: 'If there are daemon set-managed pods, drain will not proceed without --ignore-daemonsets'; --delete-emptydir-data 'Continue even if there are pods using emptyDir (local data that will be deleted when the node is drained)'; --disable-eviction 'Force drain to use delete, even if eviction is supported. This will bypass checking PodDisruptionBudgets, use with caution.' Both read through summarizing fetches on 2026-11-11 (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/generated/kubectl_drain/). The exact refusal messages in the scenario are authored renderings.

brief.situation: You are the cluster administrator at Fernhill Books (fictional), on a kubeadm cluster with one control plane node and three workers. Worker w2 rebooted at 02:00 for a kernel patch and has been NotReady since; its pods were evicted to w1 and w3, which are running hot. Worker w3 still needs the same patch and reboot in this morning's window. payments runs 3 replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable 2. Bring w2 back for good, then patch w3 without breaking payments.
handover: Last week someone added a swap file to w2's /etc/fstab while testing a database there.
You can reach every node over SSH from cp1.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, device or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command or change takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. w1 reaches memory pressure 50 minutes in if w2 is still out.

writeup.question: For the change record: why w2 was NotReady and how you made the fix stick, and how you patched w3 without breaking payments.

parts.label: Diagnosis
parts.criteria: Reads Ready Unknown as the kubelet not reporting, and finds in journalctl -u kubelet that it refuses to run with swap on.
parts.modelAnswer: describe node showed Ready Unknown, so the kubelet had stopped posting status; its journal said it would not run with swap on, because the reboot re-enabled the swap file in /etc/fstab.

parts.label: A fix that survives a reboot
parts.criteria: swapoff -a now and removes or comments the fstab entry, then restarts the kubelet and confirms Ready.
parts.modelAnswer: swapoff -a, commented the swap line in /etc/fstab so it stays off after the next boot, restarted the kubelet and watched w2 go Ready.

parts.label: Draining w3
parts.criteria: Drains w3 only once w2 can take pods, with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-emptydir-data through the eviction API so the PDB is respected; does not use --disable-eviction; reboots after the drain completes and uncordons.
parts.modelAnswer: With w2 back and schedulable, I drained w3 with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data, which respects payments' budget, rebooted it for the patch and uncordoned it. Draining while w2 was out would have stalled on the budget; --disable-eviction would have broken it.

reasoningCriteria.label: Written diagnosis, lasting fix and drain

expertPath.text: kubectl get nodes and describe node w2: Ready Unknown, kubelet stopped posting status.
On w2, the kubelet is in auto-restart; its journal says swap is on. swapon --show and /etc/fstab show the swap file.
swapoff -a, comment the fstab line, restart the kubelet; w2 goes Ready.
kubectl drain w3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data (payments moves to w2 within budget), reboot w3, uncordon w3.

fixed.headline: Good: both nodes done cleanly
fixed.body: You read the kubelet's own refusal, fixed swap now and for the next boot, and only drained w3 once w2 could take its pods.

fixedGaps.headline: Done, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: Both nodes run. The criteria show what is left: a fix that will not survive a reboot, a drain that skipped the budget, a late start or a cordon left on.

nodeWiped.headline: Node wiped
nodeWiped.body: kubeadm reset is for removing a node, not repairing one. The kubelet's journal named the problem: swap.

paymentsDown.headline: Payments broke
paymentsDown.body: A drain respects PodDisruptionBudgets only through the eviction API, and only if the pods have somewhere to go. Bring w2 back first; never --disable-eviction for a routine patch.

pressureSpread.headline: The outage spread
pressureSpread.body: Two workers carried three workers' pods until w1 gave way. journalctl -u kubelet on w2 named the fix in a minute.

stillNotReady.headline: Closed too soon
stillNotReady.body: w2's kubelet still would not start. Fix the cause, not the symptom.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Ready Unknown means the kubelet stopped posting status. journalctl -u kubelet on w2 shows it refusing to run with swap on, re-enabled from /etc/fstab by the patch reboot. Run swapoff -a, comment out the fstab line so it holds across reboots, restart the kubelet and confirm Ready. Only then drain w3 with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data so evictions respect payments' budget and land on w2, reboot w3 for its patch, and uncordon it. Never kubeadm reset a node to repair it or --disable-eviction a routine drain.
